inputs.text: They’re trying to turn a political slogan into “profanity” so schools can suppress it without admitting they’re policing dissent. The phrase’s origin is right there: a crowd was shouting “F*** Joe Biden!” and an NBC interviewer recast it as “Let’s go Brandon!” Now lower courts say schools can ban clothing that “can reasonably be interpreted as profane”—a conveniently elastic rule that lets institutions decide which messages are acceptable. The brothers’ case is headed to the U.S. Supreme Court, and the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression says their First Amendment rights were violated. This looks less like a hoodie dispute than a test of how far officials can stretch a label to silence speech they don’t want heard.
